chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: A tomboy childhood and strict upbringing
summary: She loved athletics and softball and was disciplined by a strict mother.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You've told us about school, what about recreation as a child? What kind of a child were you? Were you tomboy?
What were your friends mostly, other girls or --
Well, I had a lot of girlfriends but I guess you would say I was a tomboy
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

because I liked athletics. I used to play softball and when we'd be out playing, you know, just freakly, playing ball I remember that my brother, he was -- I recall myself protecting him when I remember one time we were at bat and when it came time to change, he didn't want to play in the field, so the boys wanted to take it out on him, you know, get -- whatever it is they call it and I recall myself taking up for him and I started fighting, fighting for my brother and the next thing I knew he was going home and left me holding the bag.

Yeah, I was a little rough for a girl, you know, when I was young. So I remember that quite vividly but we played in the school yards and we had playgrounds around. But my grandmother -- my mother's mother, she was quite strict and the only real playing that I did was like during vacation if I happened to be home in Homestead. Because during the school months I had to be in around 6 o'clock in the evening and my grandmother was strict about that. If I was some place visiting and I forgot to come home at 6 o'clock, she would get to the door and start hollering, 'Marietta!'
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
And you could hear her all over Homestead and I'd have to run home, but I don't regret it. I think it helps me quite a bit.
So you describe your upbringing as on the strict side compared to being too permissive?
